promptLatex: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$, and the vertex angle measures $m\angle A = 40^{\circ}$. What is the measure, in degrees, of $m\angle B$?
hintLatex: The two sides named in the hypothesis are equal, so the angles opposite them are equal too.
That puts one of the three interior angles at $180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ}$, and the angle asked for is half of what is left.
The two equal angles share the remaining $180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} = 140^{\circ}$, so each is $70^{\circ}$.
solutionLatex:
Since $AB = AC$, the angles opposite those sides are congruent, so $m\angle B = m\angle C$.

The angle sum gives $m\angle B + m\angle C = 180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} = 140^{\circ}$.

The two equal angles split that total, so $m\angle B = 140^{\circ} / 2 = 70^{\circ}$.
